name: Chromatin Silencing and Gene Regulation
description: Chromatin silencing in S. cerevisiae represses transcription at telomeres, HM loci (silent mating type), and rDNA through formation of heterochromatin-like structures. Sir proteins (Sir2 NAD+-dependent histone deacetylase, Sir3, Sir4) assemble at silencers, spread along chromatin by binding hypoacetylated histones, and recruit additional Sir proteins creating silent domains. Rap1 protein nucleates silencing. The process requires multiple AND gates: all Sir proteins must be present, NAD+ available for Sir2 activity, and proper chromatin context. Demonstrates eukaryotic epigenetic regulation.
scientificAccuracy: Based on decades of research on yeast silencing. All Sir proteins and mechanisms validated.
